D.treatment: digital mathematics assessment and training platforms emphasizing procedural skills
D.comparison: conceptual learning goals and deeper conceptual knowledge

O.outcome_detail: relative emphasis of platform assessment content

cells.quote: For the German-speaking school context, Thurm and Graevert (2022) analyzed the most frequently used digital assessment and training platforms for mathematics and showed that they focus nearly exclusively on procedural skills and shallow knowledge of different representations.
cells.note: The study text reports a survey finding about platform content emphasis, not learner learning outcomes; it does not state the survey design, sample expertise or age, setting details beyond the German-speaking school context, or duration.

D.treatment: looked-after children for 12 months or more

cells.quote: The most recent available statistics show that in 2017, just 2.7% of children who had been looked after for 12 months or more and 3.9% of CiN achieved the English Baccalaureate (i.e. General Certificates of Secondary Education [GCSEs] in English language and literature, maths, science, geography or history, and a language; GCSEs are sat at age 15/16 at the end of secondary schooling) compared to 21.9% of the general population.
cells.note: Descriptive cross-sectional Department for Education statistics; no adjusted comparison.

O.outcome_detail: agreement with ease, usefulness, skillfulness, and preference statements

cells.quote: Besides statement two, “Using paper/digital flashcards improved my English vocabulary,” there were higher levels of agreement in the DF group. In particular, items four, five, seven, and eight illustrated more favorable views towards DFs, with these statements receiving at least 15 percent or more agreement in the DF group than the PF group.
cells.note: The DF group showed higher agreement on most survey items, but not on the vocabulary-improvement item; no inferential test or effect size was reported.

D.comparison: digital flashcards via Quizlet and Cram

cells.quote: A much larger percentage of the students in the PF group (62%) took advantage of the opportunity to study the words outside of class compared with the DF group (31%). In fact, more than two -thirds of those studying with DFs did not study the vocabulary at all, which is nearly two times more than those who chose not to study with PFs.
cells.note: Outside-class study was encouraged but not required or tracked; time was self-reported in the post-treatment survey.
